questions.question: A list screen observes `dao.observeArticles(): Flow<List<Article>>` through the repository. The user pulls to refresh and the Retrofit call succeeds. In a single-source-of-truth design, how do the new articles reach the screen?
options: The repository writes the response into Room, the Room `Flow` re-emits, and the UI recomposes
The ViewModel replaces its list with the Retrofit response and writes to Room later in the background
The composable calls the Retrofit API itself and merges the result with the Room list
The ViewModel must call `observeArticles()` again, because a Room `Flow` emits only once
questions.explanation: With a single source of truth the network only feeds the database, and the UI only reads the database, so there is one consistent copy that also works offline. Room `Flow` queries re-emit whenever their tables change, so you don't need to query again.

questions.question: A weather app's forecast changes about once an hour. Which way of keeping it fresh is the most battery- and data-friendly?
options: Fetch on open using HTTP cache headers, plus a rare constrained WorkManager refresh if a widget needs it
Keep a WebSocket open so the server can push every change, which costs less than repeated requests
Poll the API every 30 seconds while the app is installed
Have the server send a high-priority FCM message to every user each minute, since FCM batches wakeups
questions.explanation: Data that changes hourly doesn't need a real-time channel. Every socket keep-alive, poll or high-priority push wakes the radio and drains battery. Fetching on demand plus rare, constrained background refreshes gives fresh enough data at a fraction of the cost.

questions.question: You're designing the order API for a shopping app. How should a price be represented in the JSON?
options: As an integer in minor units (e.g. `1999`) plus a currency code like `"INR"`
As a JSON number like `19.99`, parsed into a `Double` and rounded when displayed
As a pre-formatted display string like `"₹19.99"`
As a `Float`, to keep the payload smaller
questions.explanation: Binary floating point can't represent most decimal amounts exactly, so sums and comparisons drift (`0.1 + 0.2 != 0.3`). Integer minor units with an explicit currency are exact and unambiguous. A formatted string can't be computed with and bakes in one locale.

questions.question: Given `val s: String? = intent.getStringExtra("name")`, which expressions have the non-null type `String`? Select all that apply.
options: `s.orEmpty()`
`s.toString()`
`s?.trim()`
`s?.let { it }`
questions.explanation: Elvis, `orEmpty()` and `!!` all produce `String`. `toString()` is defined on `Any?`, so it also returns `String`, though it gives the text "null" for a null value, which is a classic bug. Any `?.` call keeps the result nullable, so `s?.trim()` and `s?.let { it }` are `String?`.

questions.question: After raising `targetSdk` to 35, a Compose screen's top title draws under the status bar and its bottom button sits under the gesture navigation bar. What is the right fix?
options: Consume window insets, e.g. `Scaffold`'s `innerPadding` or `windowInsetsPadding(WindowInsets.safeDrawing)`
Hard-code `24.dp` top and `48.dp` bottom padding, which matches the standard bar heights on most devices
Set `windowOptOutEdgeToEdgeEnforcement` in the theme, which permanently restores the pre-35 layout
Lower `targetSdk` back to 34 to keep the old layout
questions.explanation: Apps targeting Android 15 are drawn edge-to-edge, so content has to consume the system bar and cutout insets. Bar sizes vary by device and navigation mode, so hard-coded padding breaks. The opt-out attribute is deprecated and ignored once you target 36, and Play's target-SDK rules rule out staying on an old target.

questions.question: The screen collects `prices` with `collectAsStateWithLifecycle()`. The user presses Home and leaves the app in the background for an hour, and the process isn't killed. What happens to the polling loop?
options: It keeps polling every 5 seconds all hour, since `Eagerly` ties the upstream to `viewModelScope`
It stops when the screen goes to STOPPED, because `collectAsStateWithLifecycle` cancels the upstream flow
It pauses because `viewModelScope` is suspended while the app is in the background
It stops after 5 seconds, because `stateIn` waits for the delay timeout
questions.explanation: Lifecycle-aware collection only stops the UI's subscription. With `Eagerly` the shared upstream runs for as long as `viewModelScope` lives, and the ViewModel survives in the background. `SharingStarted.WhileSubscribed(5_000)` would stop the polling a few seconds after the last collector leaves.

questions.question: Polling an endpoint every minute with `If-None-Match` is cheap on battery, because an unchanged resource returns `304 Not Modified` with no body.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: A `304` saves bytes and parsing, but each poll still wakes the cellular radio, which then stays in a high-power state for several seconds afterwards. That wake-up, not the payload, dominates the energy cost, so frequent polling is expensive even when nothing changed. Push, or less frequent batched fetches, fix it.

questions.question: `PaymentState` is a sealed interface. A teammate adds a new `Refunded` subtype, and the project still compiles with no warnings. Screens render it like this. What's going on?
options: The `else` branch silently swallows `Refunded`; without it, the compiler would flag each unhandled `when`
Sealed hierarchies are only checked for exhaustiveness at runtime, so a crash is coming
The compiler routes `Refunded` to the nearest matching branch, `Paid`, by declaration order
`when` on a sealed type must always have an `else`, so this is the recommended pattern
questions.explanation: Exhaustiveness checking is the main benefit of sealed types. Listing every subtype without `else` turns adding a new state into a compile error at each place that needs updating. A catch-all `else` gives that up and hides new cases.

questions.question: Which statements about runtime permissions on current Android are true? Select all that apply.
options: Apps targeting Android 13+ must request `POST_NOTIFICATIONS` at runtime before their notifications are shown
The recommended way to request a permission is an `ActivityResultContracts.RequestPermission` launcher
`ACCESS_BACKGROUND_LOCATION` must be requested separately, after foreground location has been granted
`INTERNET` is a dangerous permission, so the user is prompted before the first network call
Once granted, a permission stays granted forever and the app never needs to check it again
questions.explanation: Notifications are opt-in from Android 13, the Activity Result API replaced `onRequestPermissionsResult`, and background location is a separate, later request. `INTERNET` is a normal install-time permission. Grants can be one-time, revoked in Settings or auto-reset for unused apps, so check with `checkSelfPermission` each time.

questions.question: What happens when you compile this file?
questions.code:
typealias UserId = String
@JvmInline value class OrderId(val raw: String)

fun load(id: String) = "string"
fun load(id: UserId) = "user"
fun load(id: OrderId) = "order"
options: It fails with conflicting overloads for the `String` and `UserId` versions. The `OrderId` overload is fine
It compiles, and Kotlin picks the overload based on the alias name
It fails for all three, because `OrderId` is also just a `String` at runtime
It fails only for the `OrderId` overload, because value classes can't be parameters of overloaded functions
questions.explanation: A `typealias` is just another name for the same type, so `load(UserId)` is the same signature as `load(String)`. A value class is a distinct type at compile time, and its JVM name is mangled so it doesn't clash with `String`, even though it's unboxed at runtime.

questions.question: Two different Navigation destinations each call `hiltViewModel<DetailViewModel>()` with no arguments. While both are on the back stack, they share the same `DetailViewModel` instance.
options: True
False
questions.explanation: Inside a `NavHost`, each back stack entry is its own `ViewModelStoreOwner`, so each destination gets its own instance, cleared when that entry is popped. To share one, pass a common owner such as the parent graph's back stack entry.

questions.question: What does this print?
questions.code:
data class Key(var id: Int)

fun main() {
    val k = Key(1)
    val map = hashMapOf(k to "cached")
    k.id = 2
    println("${map[k]} ${map[Key(1)]} ${map.size}")
}
options: null null 1
cached null 1
null cached 1
cached cached 1
questions.explanation: The entry was stored in the bucket for `hashCode()` 1. After the mutation, `map[k]` searches the bucket for hash 2 and finds nothing. `map[Key(1)]` finds the right bucket, but `equals` fails because the stored key now has id 2. The entry is still there (size 1) but can't be reached, which is why hash keys should be immutable.

questions.question: You need to rename a JSON field from `user_name` to `username`. Old app versions stay installed for months and can't be force-upgraded. What's the safest rollout?
options: Send both fields, ship clients reading `username` (fallback `user_name`), and drop `user_name` once old traffic is negligible
Rename the field on the server and release the app update the same day, so both change together
Raise the minimum supported version right away so every user has to update before the rename
Create a `/v2` copy of the whole API for this one field
questions.explanation: This is the expand-and-contract pattern: add the new field, migrate the clients, and remove the old field once nobody reads it. Renaming in place breaks every installed old version, a forced update is a heavy hammer for a cosmetic change, and a whole new API version adds lasting maintenance cost for one field.

questions.question: Which of these are safe to call directly inside `viewModelScope.launch { }` (which runs on `Dispatchers.Main`) without wrapping them in `withContext`? Select all that apply.
options: A Retrofit `suspend fun getUser(): User`
A Room DAO `suspend fun insert(user: User)`
`dataStore.data.first()`
A non-suspend Room DAO `fun getAll(): List<User>`
`File(cacheDir, "feed.json").readText()` on a 2 MB file
`Json.decodeFromString<Feed>(hugeString)` on a 5 MB payload
questions.explanation: Retrofit, Room and DataStore suspend APIs are main-safe because they move their own work off the main thread. A blocking Room DAO called on the main thread throws `IllegalStateException`, file I/O blocks it, and decoding a large payload is CPU work, so those need `withContext(Dispatchers.IO)` or `Dispatchers.Default`.

questions.question: In a keyed `LazyColumn`, each row holds `var a by remember { mutableStateOf(false) }` and `var b by rememberSaveable { mutableStateOf(false) }`. The user sets both to `true` on row 3, scrolls far down so the row is disposed, then scrolls back. What does row 3 show?
options: `a` is `false` again and `b` is still `true`
Both are still `true`, because `LazyColumn` caches every row it has composed
Both are `false`, because `rememberSaveable` only survives configuration changes
`a` is `true` and `b` is `false`, because the saved state is restored only after rotation
questions.explanation: A row that scrolls out of the viewport leaves the composition, so its `remember` state is lost. Lazy layouts save each item's `rememberSaveable` state under the item key and restore it when the item comes back. State that really matters, like a selection, should be hoisted into the ViewModel anyway.

questions.question: The last one: a running total of the study plan, one value per track. What does this print?
questions.explanation: `scan` emits its seed 0 and then each running total, and `filter` drops the 0. `days` is a cold flow, so `reduce` and `last` each collect it from scratch and `onStart` runs twice, which is why "go" prints twice. Congratulations, that's all 60 days!
